notes.text: Kasperi Kapanen has started playing on the power play: on the ice for 51% of the team’s power-play time in 20 games, up from 6% last season.
Ty Emberson is no longer killing penalties: 3% of the team’s shorthanded time in 16 games, down from 30% last season.

Kirill Marchenko is on injured reserve and has missed the last 7 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Easton Cowan has taken his spot beside Jack Roslovic and Auston Matthews. That line has had 51% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 47:37 together, down from 72% with Marchenko.

Nick Blankenburg is out week to week (upper body injury) and has missed the last 9 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Troy Stecher has taken his spot beside Oliver Ekman-Larsson. That pair has had 59% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 59:20 together, up from 48% with Blankenburg.
Morgan Rielly is day to day (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 3 games. He is a top-pair defenseman. Oliver Ekman-Larsson has taken his spot beside Troy Stecher.
Ryan Tverberg was added to the roster on Nov 12 and has played beside John Tavares and William Nylander.
Oliver Ekman-Larsson has started killing penalties: on the ice for 30% of the team’s shorthanded time in 21 games, up from 6% last season.

TOR.head: Close, but the Oilers have the slight edge
TOR.body: Even though Toronto has home-ice advantage and gets Tanev back, Edmonton has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. On top of that, Toronto will be without Marchenko. The Maple Leafs can tip it if they keep dangerous shots away.

EDM.head: Leaning the Oilers’ way
EDM.body: Even though Toronto has home-ice advantage and gets Tanev back, Edmonton has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. On top of that, Toronto will be without Marchenko. Still, it’s close: the Maple Leafs can make it interesting if they keep dangerous shots away.

story.head: The Maple Leafs need a win
paras: The Maple Leafs won the teams’ first meeting this season, 7-2 in Edmonton on Oct 24. The Maple Leafs are on a five-game losing streak, while the Oilers have won three straight. Going in, the Oilers are first in the Pacific (third in the NHL) and the Leafs seventh in the Atlantic (tied for 23rd).
The Oilers’ record (.775) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.574), largely thanks to their finishing. The Maple Leafs’ record (.429) is about what their chances are worth.

The Oilers lean on their stars more than any team in the league (lowest) and ice the puck less than almost anyone (2nd). They also have one of the league’s most dangerous power plays (2nd), and that could do real damage against the Maple Leafs’ penalty kill (27th). Edmonton has scored 4.00 goals a game, the third most in the league. On the other side, the Maple Leafs get their shots through better than anyone (1st), but take more penalties than they draw (32nd) and have had shaky goaltending (31st). The Oilers have the edge over the Maple Leafs on shot suppression.

Connor McDavid (11 G / 38 A / 49 P in 20 GP) leads the Oilers and the whole NHL in scoring, with ten points in his last five games. Leon Draisaitl (18 G / 19 A / 37 P in 20 GP) has a team-high 18 goals, the most in the NHL, with nine points in his last five games and five goals in seven games against Toronto since 2023-24. Auston Matthews (12 G / 17 A / 29 P in 21 GP) leads the Maple Leafs in scoring and is sixth in the NHL, and William Nylander (11 G / 11 A / 22 P in 21 GP) is next in line.

Sergei Bobrovsky (3-8-2 / .881 SV% in 13 GS) will likely start for Toronto. Edmonton has two options in net: Tristan Jarry (5-1-3 / .903 SV% in 9 GS) and Devon Levi (8-1-0 / .898 SV% in 9 GS). Jarry has started six of their last ten games, including the last one on Wednesday, so Edmonton could turn to Levi to give him a rest. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
